close_reason: Rewrote all 10 named bd:JMAP-* leak sites in backend.rs/lib.rs/permissions.rs as self-contained statements of the rule each reference represented (option 2 in the bead recommendation — 'better' path). Verified clean via grep against the 3 named files. Broader-scope sites in space.rs and memory.rs (which the bead did not enumerate but the grep surfaced) filed as JMAP-x2gd.98 follow-up rather than silently expanded into this bead's scope. description:
## Finding

The published rustdoc for jmap-chat-server references the internal
Beads issue tracker (`bd:JMAP-*` identifiers) in **10 locations**
spread across three files. These appear inside `///` doc comments,
not `//` source comments, meaning they render in `cargo doc` and
will appear on `docs.rs/jmap-chat-server` for any third-party
consumer.

Locations (verified via grep):

- src/backend.rs:398 — \"See bd:JMAP-sc1b.89\"
- src/backend.rs:409 — \"See bd:JMAP-x2gd.36 follow-ups\"
- src/backend.rs:464 — \"\`bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.7\` and are NOT yet applied\"
- src/backend.rs:470 — \"it calls this method (bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.8)\"
- src/backend.rs:487 — \"\`bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3\`\"
- src/backend.rs:566 — \"this method landed in bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.13\"
- src/backend.rs:590 — \"(bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.12)\"
- src/backend.rs:612 — \"\`bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3\`\"
- src/lib.rs:44 — \"(bd:JMAP-ga0q)\"
- src/permissions.rs:102 — \"see bd:JMAP-x2gd.37\"

## What goes wrong for a third-party caller

A third-party implementer reading the published docs has **no
way to dereference \`bd:JMAP-*\` identifiers** — the Beads tracker
is a workspace-local sqlite database not exposed publicly. They
see opaque identifiers and either:

1. Conclude the bead is a normative reference (it isn't — it's
   an internal tracker).
2. Conclude something is \"not yet applied\" without knowing how
   to tell when it lands (the rustdoc at backend.rs:464 literally
   says \"NOT yet applied by the reference handler\" with no
   externally-resolvable forward pointer).
3. Try to grep the published source for the identifier and find
   it only in other doc comments, creating a circular reference.

The most consequential case is backend.rs:464 — `apply_space_patch`'s
permission-gate-status note tells the implementer \"handler-side
gates tracked in \`bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.7\` and are NOT yet applied.\"
That's a stale, externally-unresolvable status note in the
published contract for a P0-importance method.

## What this looks like to a consumer

On docs.rs the strings render verbatim. A consumer at
docs.rs/jmap-chat-server/latest/jmap_chat_server/backend/trait.ChatBackend.html
sees \"bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3\" as text. There is no link, no
explanation, and no externally-resolvable reference. This is a
contract leak: the published doc surface tells consumers about
internal workflow state they cannot consume.

## Recommendation

Two paths, in order of cost:

1. **Cheap:** strip bd:JMAP-* references from doc comments before
   publish, keep them in source comments (`//`) only. Each line
   converts to either a self-contained statement of the rule or
   an issue-tracker pointer at the workspace's public GitHub
   repo.

2. **Better:** replace each \`bd:JMAP-*\` reference with a
   self-contained statement of the rule it represents, so the
   doc no longer relies on an external bookkeeping system for
   meaning. e.g. \`bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.3\` → \"see the role-hierarchy
   rule in draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §X.Y\" or \"see
   \`MemoryBackend::set_protect_last_admin_for_test\`\".

## Engineering basis

Direct verification: \`grep -n \"bd:JMAP-\" src/backend.rs
src/lib.rs src/permissions.rs\` returns the 10 hits cited
above, all inside \`///\` doc-comment context (verified by
inspection of each cited line).
title: API contract: bd:JMAP-* internal beads tracker IDs embedded in 10 published-rustdoc locations
